第 36 章 Good Process Is Evolved, Not Designed好流程是演进出来的，不是设计出来的

Will Larson / 威尔·拉尔森

— 第 110 页 —

Time management is an ongoing challenge for managers. Although there can be a certain heady rush to being relentlessly busy, I'm convinced that far more senior managers are overwhelmed with work than they want to be. What's a bit scary to contemplate is that they're overwhelmed by work generated from processes that they themselves were heavily involved in designing.

时间管理对经理来说是持续的挑战。虽然无情地忙碌可能有一种让人兴奋的快感，但我相信更多高级经理被工作压得喘不过气，超出了他们想要的程度。有点可怕的是，他们被自己深度参与设计的流程产生的工作压得喘不过气。

Process design is a foundational skill for well-run organizations, yet is often treated as an afterthought. Individual processes garner a great deal of attention, but we rarely speak about how to create process effectively. The good news is that success here doesn't require innovation or novelty: adopt a structured approach and you'll quickly become an effective process designer.

流程设计是良好运转组织的基础技能，但经常被当成事后才想起来的事。单个流程获得大量关注，但我们很少讨论如何有效地创建流程。好消息是这里的成功不需要创新或新奇：采用结构化方法，你很快就会成为有效的流程设计者。

How to Evolve Process如何演进流程

When we talk about creating a process, we almost always say that we designed a process. Design is a great word, because it implies the kind of careful thoughtfulness that great process does indeed possess. However, it's also a misleading word, because great process never emerges from the Feynman algorithm ("write down the problem, think very hard, write down the solution"), but instead derives from guided evolution.

当我们谈论创建流程时，我们几乎总是说我们设计了一个流程。设计是个好词，因为它暗示了好的流程确实具备的那种深思熟虑。然而它也是一个误导性的词，因为好的流程从来不是从费曼算法（「写下问题，努力思考，写下答案」）中产生的，而是从有引导的演进中得来的。

Here's the algorithm that I've found effective:

以下是我发现有效的算法：

  1. Identify problem statement. There is a problem that either you have identified or folks you support have raised. Refine this into a problem statement that captures the problem you want to solve along with the constraints you want to respect while doing so.识别问题陈述。有一个你或你支持的人提出的问题。把它提炼成一个问题陈述，抓住你想解决的问题以及你想尊重的约束。
  2. Document approaches. It's easy to simply apply the approaches you're most familiar with; so easy, in fact, that it's the most prevalent failure mode of leaders who join a new company. Take some time to reach out to folks at other companies and learn how they approach the same problem.记录方法。简单应用你最熟悉的方法很容易——容易到这实际上是加入新公司的领导者最常见的失败模式。花时间联系其他公司的人，了解他们怎么处理同样的问题。
  3. Test approach. Identify a reasonable approach, not necessarily an amazing one, and give it a limited test run. The best test run is cheap and narrow, optimizing for rapid feedback over a perfect approach.测试方法。选一个合理的方法，不一定是惊艳的，做一个有限的试运行。最好的试运行是便宜且狭窄的，优化快速反馈而不是完美方法。
  4. Iterate approach. With your updated problem statement, adapt or replace your approach with another reasonable idea. Then, return to testing it!迭代方法。用更新后的问题陈述，调整或替换你的方法为另一个合理想法。然后回到测试！
  5. Practice. After you find an approach that works reasonably well, folks often want to begin evaluating it immediately, but that's often ineffective. The first time an organization uses a new process almost never goes super well; it takes time to learn new things, particularly when you need hundreds of folks to change at the same time.练习。在你找到一个合理有效的方法后，人们经常想立刻开始评估，但这通常无效。组织第一次用新流程几乎不会特别顺利；学习新事物需要时间，尤其是你需要几百人同时改变时。
— 第 111 页 —

So now we have an algorithm for designing process, but honestly you already knew this was the best way to design process. That's the most interesting discovery when chatting with folks about how to design process: they already know how.

现在我们有了设计流程的算法，但老实说你早就知道这是设计流程的最好方式。和人聊怎么设计流程时最有趣的发现是：他们已经知道怎么做了。

Why, in that case, do we keep making ineffective processes?

那既然如此，我们为什么还在不断做无效的流程？

Why Good People Make Bad Process为什么好人做出坏流程

Almost every bad process I've encountered has had the same problem: the problem statement is wrong. At best this leads to inert processes that solve scenarios that don't exist; at worst they're overactive, causing great inconvenience while doing little good. A common example in Silicon Valley companies is wanting to manage operations teams with a "churn and burn" mentality, but also wanting to be a company that inspires loyalty and high retention. This can lead to statements emphasizing ongoing education and career mobility coupled with processes that hinder such development.

我遇到的几乎每个坏流程都有同样的问题：问题陈述是错的。最好的情况是导致解决不存在场景的惰性流程；最坏的情况是它们过度活跃，造成极大不便却几乎没什么好处。硅谷公司的一个常见例子是想用「 churn and burn 」心态管理运营团队，但又想成为一个激发忠诚和高留任率的公司。这会导致强调持续教育和职业流动的声明，加上阻碍这种发展的流程。

— 第 112 页 —

Designing great process requires honest alignment on goals, methodical approach, and a great deal of thoughtful attention. Without all three, you'll rarely enact great process, and in the rare case where you do, it will decay quickly across context changes. That's the bad news, but the good news is that great process builds momentum for more great process. The time you spend evolving it will come back to you, which makes evolving good process the single highest leverage act of management.

设计好的流程需要在目标上的诚实对齐、有条理的方法、以及大量深思熟虑的关注。没有这三者，你很少能制定好的流程，即使极少数情况下做到了，它也会在上下文变化中迅速衰退。这是坏消息，但好消息是好流程会为更多好流程建立动力。你花在演进它上的时间会回报给你，这让演进好流程成为管理中最高杠杆的行为。
